value.title: Role send follow-ups (s05 dogfood)
value.summary: Fix what the s05 dogfood found: the role-address refusal loop (F52), a silent drain on assign (F56), no way to see or withdraw a queued request (F59), the window rename on release (F57), and the shim's gaps around role sends (F53, F54, F55, F58).

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Source: governance roles/docs-system/outputs/2026-11/dogfood-s05.md (lungfish, 06 Nov). s05 shipped in #129 (dc9f2e4). The shim gaps overlap plan 209's F41-F44 and F50; coordinate so each fix lands once (209 owns the generic human-output rendering; this plan owns the role-send specifics).

sections.name: goals
value: Fix what the s05 dogfood found: the role-address refusal loop (F52), a silent drain on assign (F56), no way to see or withdraw a queued request (F59), the window rename on release (F57), and the shim's gaps around role sends (F53, F54, F55, F58).

sections.name: non_goals
value: Anything another roadmap step owns; see roadmap 001.

value.claim: F52, the refusal loop. E-RS-ROLE-HOLDERS (several holders) and E-RS-ROLE-ADDRESS (an instance on a role whose holders have no instances) never advise each other in a loop: the several-holders refusal lists each holder with its instance, or says the holders have no instances and gives the runnable fix (assign per-PR instances: pij directory assign <role>/<instance> <seat>); next is never null.
F56, drain on assign is visible. The assign receipt lists the requests it drained (id, requester, reply mode), in human and --json output.

F59, list and withdraw. `pij requests [--role <id>] [--state queued|delivering|delivered]` lists role requests; `pij requests withdraw <id> --why <text>` withdraws a queued one (requester, the PA or the prime only).
F57, windows. Releasing a holding restores the window name the assign replaced (or the seat's default) when the seat holds no other role.

Shim parity for role sends (F53, F54, F55, F58). pij send --help shows role:<id>[/<instance>], --reply and --fyi; the human receipt prints the request id and reply mode; --body is accepted (or the help and every printed command say positional or --body-file only); directory add prints the human form.
Cost (AGENTS.md, resource cost is a correctness property). No new timer, poll or launch site. List and withdraw are store reads and writes; the receipt and window changes are in-process.

Docs and states. No workstream state changes (follow-ups); docs/how/pij-rs-api.md documents pij requests and the new receipt fields. docs/how/pij-rs-api.md documents new verbs and refusals; the skill's verb coverage tables carry them; `just ddocs-check` and `ddocs validate` on the project docs pass; the PR body has a `Delivers:` line.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: Code to read first: crates/daemon/src/delivery/role_send.rs, crates/daemon/src/http/role_send.rs, crates/store/src/role_requests.rs, the directory assign and release paths (window rename), and the pij shim (.omp or npm shim, wherever pij send's human output is rendered). Migration only if withdraw needs a state; 0034 is merged, so claim the next number with pij claim migration.

value.risk: Two lanes edit the same CLI wiring or skill files.
value.mitigation: Rebase onto main before the PR; small diffs at the seam; pm-001 orders merges.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Tests use scratch repos and a private daemon; never the live governance branch or the prod daemon.
Builds: your own target or `just shared-build`; CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; -p scoping; stop under 25 GB free.
No `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`; no node_modules, never symlinked (C25); TS proof is CI on the exact head.
Shared seams (crates/cli wiring, skills/pij): rebase onto main before the PR and keep edits minimal; don't fork the seam.
One push per review round; no pushes after the PR is out for verdicts unless a verdict asks.
